perspective:
Gloria’s accessible information:

- She works as an administrative assistant at a large event-planning company and knows Donald as a colleague/bartender at company events.
- Over several company events, she observed Donald serving drinks with little enthusiasm and a distracted demeanor; she believed he might be unhappy with the job.
- In their first conversation, she asked if he was okay. Donald told her he was not as into the job as before and found it repetitive.
- Afterward, she suspected his job dissatisfaction might be tied to larger personal issues. She suggested he consider talking to a professional. Donald told her he hadn’t considered it and wasn’t sure it would help.
- Later, she sensed a change in Donald’s behavior toward her and believed he might resent her suggestion as overstepping. She apologized, saying she cared and did not mean to overstep or make assumptions. Donald told her it was okay, that he was taken aback at first, knew she meant well, and that it was a lot to process.
- She felt relieved that the apology was well received and tension eased. She invited Donald to collaborate on a new project. Donald thanked her, said he appreciated it, wanted to be more involved, and thought it sounded like a great opportunity.
- After the collaboration, she observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm; she believed he was valuable and decided to make sure he felt appreciated.
- At a meeting, she publicly acknowledged Donald’s incredible and crucial work on the project. Donald thanked her, said it meant a lot, was glad to contribute, and felt appreciated.
